headline: Utah buys Jazz gear five kids at a time, dressed for the canyon and measured against Stockton and Malone.
thesis: Jazz fans drive in from Ogden, Logan, Provo, St. George, southern Idaho and Wyoming, and they buy as families, kids first. Taste comes from a thin layer: the all-ages DIY scene in Sugar House and the Granary District, and West Side Pacific Islander and Latino families. Those families rank church-ward, rec and high school basketball with football. The Stockton-Malone-Sloan era is the moral standard, a younger crowd grew up on the Mitchell-Gobert playoff years, and everyone wears technical outdoor layers as everyday clothes. The City Edition is a gray-gradient repeat and there's no opening-night, Christmas or Specter stage, so the Oct 30 home Cup night against Denver is the one fixed date. Land a Peterson-and-Bailey family program before the Oct 20 tip-off, then sell it as a local family gift through the Cup nights to Three Kings Day. After that, turn the gray gradient into Utah material in Nike's own cold-weather layers, and pitch Salt Line now as the 2027-28 City Edition.

archetype.name: The Statewide Family Loyalist
archetype.description: A fan who drives in on I-15 with three kids in purple youth jerseys and measures every new star against Stockton and Malone. The January walk to the Delta Center is cold, so it's a puffer and a beanie. Loyal to the team over any brand, patient with a rebuild, allergic to hype.

pulse.teamMoment: Coming off 22-60, Utah is speeding up its youth movement. No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey join Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Walker Kessler went to the Lakers for future firsts, and Jaxson Hayes and Josh Okogie came in. Will Hardy is under pressure to develop them, and BetMGM's 35.5-win total asks for about 13 more wins.
pulse.sentiment: Impatient but curious. Fans are tired after a bottom-of-the-league year and energized by Peterson and the Jackson Jr. trade. They expect visible progress and a play-in chase, not a playoff run.

topInsights.title: The repeat City Edition needs new material
topInsights.insight: The vertical gray gradient with baby blue trim is back for a second straight season, so there's no debut spike to sell. Every lens maps that gray onto something locals live with: winter inversion haze, Wasatch granite, the salt crust of the Bonneville flats, a clear high-desert sky after a storm.
topInsights.implication: Texture is the refresh: salt-crackle print, granite-speckle fleece, inversion-to-sky fades. Never market it as new, and save the big story for the next City Edition.

topInsights.title: Buy for five kids, not one collector
topInsights.insight: Utah has the largest average household and the youngest median age of any state. Families buy Jazz gear in multiples, on a once-a-season trip to the Delta Center, a Murray or Orem mall, or Dick's. Deseret Industries thrifting and value-tier buying are normal. Authentic jerseys are a small collector niche.
topInsights.implication: Lead with deep youth and toddler sizing in the current Mountain Purple, black and sky blue palette. Add matching kid-to-adult sets and bundle-friendly entry tees. Keep premium to a small tier, clearly set apart.

topInsights.title: Canyon wardrobe is game-night wardrobe
topInsights.insight: Locals ski Alta, Snowbird and Brighton after work and hoop in cold church and rec-center gyms all winter. Technical shells, fleece and snap-pocket layers are everyday clothes. From November through March, fans head to the Delta Center in puffers, fleece and beanies.
topInsights.implication: Outerwear and layering belong at the core of the Jazz assortment, inside Nike's own ACG and NBA outerwear lanes. Borrow local technical codes (shell cuts, snap pockets, drawcords) instead of partnering with outdoor competitors.

topInsights.title: Three eras and an untold origin
topInsights.insight: Fans split into Note-era (1979-96) and 1996 Mountain-era loyalists, and younger fans thrift both at DI and cut them up. Fans now in their 20s grew up on the 2017-22 Donovan Mitchell and Rudy Gobert playoff teams. Everyone knows the 'no jazz in Utah' joke and the New Orleans start, but no product tells it well.
topInsights.implication: Run separate era capsules instead of mixing palettes, with a Mitchell-Gobert chapter that bridges to Peterson. Put the New Orleans origin on labels and inserts with the team mark, not a player name. First, confirm which licensee holds heritage jerseys.

topInsights.title: The West Side: big on hoops, barely served
topInsights.insight: Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns hold one of the highest per-capita Pacific Islander populations in the US, plus large Latino communities. They're a major part of the valley's youth basketball and football, from church-ward leagues to high school programs. Yet they have few premium doors and appear on almost no Jazz product.
topInsights.implication: Co-create a capsule with paid, credited Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers, each community with its own credit and approval rights. Use PIK2AR and Centro Civico Mexicano for cultural review and access, not as design studios. Never lift tatau, tapa or ceremonial patterns.

topInsights.title: Utah taste grew up all-ages
topInsights.insight: Utah is young and has few under-21 rooms, so its scene grew up in all-ages venues like Kilby Court. SLUG Magazine documented it, and SLUG's screen-printed flyers and Gallery Stroll openings are the local graphic language.
topInsights.implication: The lifestyle graphic language is gig-poster screen prints, hand-lettered date blocks and cassette and 7-inch packaging, in Jazz purple, black and sky blue inks. Keep bar imagery and jokes about the state's religious culture off the line.

topInsights.title: One fixed stage, then local quiet zones
topInsights.insight: The Jazz aren't on the opening-night or Christmas slate, so the confirmed Oct 30 home Cup night against Denver is the season's only fixed in-arena stage. General Conference empties the first weekends of April and October. Many households keep Sunday as a family day, and Halloween is a major neighborhood night. In summer, July 24 Pioneer Day outranks any NBA date.
topInsights.implication: Tie the launch to dates already certain: product in doors by Sat Oct 17, the Oct 30 Cup night, Black Friday. Stage in-person drops on Fridays and Saturdays, and avoid Oct 31. Push Sunday demand to digital, and run December to Jan 6 as local family gifting.

opportunities.title: Peterson-Bailey Family Pack
opportunities.summary: A youth-first player program and Valley gift ladder for households with several kids. Peterson and Bailey youth jerseys and tees, toddler sizes and matching kid-to-adult sets land before tip-off and sell as gifts through Three Kings Day.
where: Jazz and Nike e-commerce for out-of-metro fans
opportunities.when: In doors by Sat Oct 17, peaking at the Oct 30 Cup night and Black Friday, and gifted through Jan 6
opportunities.how: Stock deeper on Peterson and Bailey than on legacy names. Markkanen and Jackson Jr. are the adult core (his jersey is new to most fans), all in the current purple Icon and black Statement looks. Clear leftover Kessler stock before launch. Ladder it good-better-best for families of four or five, with bundle pricing and a Jazz Bear hook for kids. Launch in-store on Saturday Oct 17, never a Sunday. Stretch the gift window to Jan 6 in West Side doors and at Centro Civico Mexicano events for Latino families.
products: Markkanen and Jackson Jr. adult player hoodies
opportunities.segment: Families and youth across the Wasatch Front
opportunities.kpi: Youth and kids' share of Jazz units, and multi-unit basket rate at the team store and Murray and Orem doors from Oct 17 to Jan 6

opportunities.title: Inversion Layer Cold-Weather Line
opportunities.summary: The repeat City Edition, reframed as Utah material. It's a Nike-only gray-to-baby-blue outerwear and fleece line with salt-crackle and granite-speckle textures, built for the canyon commute and the walk into the Delta Center.
opportunities.when: Launch with ski-resort openings in mid-to-late November and sell through spring skiing
opportunities.how: Tell the inversion-haze-to-clear-sky story on hangtags and in-store. Build within ACG and NBA outerwear using local technical codes (shell cut, snap pockets, drawcords), with no outside brand. Sell it as the Christmas gift for the fan who skis. The salt-crackle print doubles as the first fan test of the Salt Line City Edition texture. If resort openings slip or a warm November stalls demand, hold the launch to Black Friday and sell it as a gift through e-commerce and the Murray and Orem doors.
opportunities.kpi: City Edition outerwear sell-through by Jan 31 and attach rate of beanies and vests to jersey purchases

opportunities.title: Group A Cup Nights
opportunities.summary: A dated Cup kit for the two home Group A nights, led by the confirmed Fri Oct 30 game against Denver. A pre-approved knockout hoodie prints only if Utah advances.
where: Delta Center team store and plaza
Fashion Place, Murray and University Place, Orem (Saturday carryover)
opportunities.when: Fri Oct 30 vs. Denver, the second home Group A night once the schedule names it, and the Dec 4-9 knockout window
opportunities.how: Oct 30 is the rookies' first Cup game: at home, against Northwest Division neighbor Denver, on a Friday that suits the family trip. Sell a dated Group A tee beside the family pack, and drop poster tee No. 1 at Kilby Court the same night. Repeat with an opponent-dated tee on the second home night (Houston, Phoenix or Dallas). Hold a knockout hoodie blank that prints within 48 hours, only for a Dec 4-5 quarterfinal or a home Dec 8-9 semifinal. If Utah is out, the blanks become the December poster tee.
products: Group A Cup night tee, dated vs. Denver
opportunities.segment: Families on their once-a-season Friday trip and Gen Z fans
opportunities.kpi: Units per attendee on the two home Cup nights against a normal Friday home game, and knockout-hoodie turnaround under 48 hours if triggered

opportunities.title: West Side Court Collective
opportunities.summary: A capsule co-designed with Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers from Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns. It sells at community events and named West Side doors, and it funds youth rec basketball.
where: Sorenson Unity Center and community courts in Glendale and Rose Park
Valley Fair Mall, West Valley City (confirm door)
opportunities.when: Commission in winter, reveal at Living Traditions in May, sell through the park-court season and Hispanic Heritage Month
opportunities.how: Recruit and pay designers through the Salt Lake Arts Council's artist networks and a Latino arts partner such as Mestizo Institute of Culture and Arts. Pay PIK2AR and Centro Civico Mexicano as cultural reviewers. Give Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers separate credit and approval, and route a share of proceeds to West Side rec leagues. Launch court-side, not downtown. If no West Valley door is confirmed or Living Traditions moves, sell through the partners' own events and reveal at Centro Civico Mexicano in late May.
opportunities.segment: Pacific Islander and Latino hoop families on the West Side
opportunities.kpi: Number of paid local collaborators, sell-through at community events and the named West Side door, and dollars delivered to youth rec programs

opportunities.title: Delta Night Poster Series
opportunities.summary: One screen-printed gig-poster tee per month of home games, packaged like a 7-inch single. Local poster artists and printers make them in the Kilby Court and SLUG Magazine tradition.
opportunities.when: First drop at Kilby Court on Fri Oct 30 (the Nuggets Cup night), then monthly on Gallery Stroll Fridays through April
opportunities.how: Commission a different Utah artist each month through Craft Lake City and SLUG. Print locally in limited runs, with off-register ink in Jazz purple, black and sky blue plus newsprint cream, and release on Gallery Stroll Fridays. The Jan 15 poster tests land-speed numerals and a thin lake-pink line, the fan check before Salt Line is signed off. A sleeve-style hangtag carries a local-artist playlist QR.
opportunities.segment: Gen Z and Sugar House creative fans
opportunities.kpi: Sell-out time per monthly run and social mentions from local scene accounts

opportunities.title: Note Era and Mountain Era Capsules
opportunities.summary: Separate heritage capsules for the 1979-96 Note, the 1996 Mountain look and the 2017-22 Mitchell-Gobert playoff years. Labels and inserts tell the New Orleans origin.
where: Delta Center team store on legend nights
opportunities.when: December gifting is the anchor. A second push follows on a legend or throwback night if the schedule has one, otherwise in the February All-Star lull.
opportunities.how: Confirm which licensee holds Note and Mountain heritage jerseys before promising one. Nike leads tees, fleece and warm-ups under team and NBA licensing. Use the team mark for the New Orleans chapter, and clear any player names through the NBPA or estates. Bridge to the rookies with a Peterson tee in an era palette.
opportunities.segment: Heritage diehards and parents buying for kids
opportunities.kpi: Heritage share of adult apparel revenue and repeat purchase among heritage buyers

opportunities.title: I-15 Saturday Pop-ups
opportunities.summary: Saturday pop-ups in Ogden and Provo-Orem let fans who reach the Delta Center only once a season buy close to home. Salt Lake City Stars G League games add an entry-price door.
where: Salt Lake City Stars home games
opportunities.when: Saturdays from Nov 7 through the gifting season, never Halloween or a Sunday
opportunities.how: Rotate a mobile shop through the corridor stops, Saturdays only, starting Nov 7. Bring the Jazz Bear for kids, and sell a stop-exclusive cap with the stop's own name in Jazz colors, never a college color. Add a family-priced table at Stars games. Send Sunday and General Conference shoppers to e-commerce.
opportunities.segment: Statewide and rural fans and Utah County families
opportunities.kpi: Pop-up revenue per stop and share of buyers who have not visited the Delta Center this season

opportunities.title: Draft Night to Speed Week
opportunities.summary: This fan base follows prospects all year, so own the offseason. Start with a draft-night rookie tee and one Salt Lake City Summer League pop-up, then an August land-speed numeral tee that previews Salt Line.
where: Craft Lake City DIY Fest, Utah State Fairpark
opportunities.when: Late June draft through mid-July Summer League, then Speed Week and DIY Fest in mid-August
opportunities.how: Print the new pick's tee within hours of draft night. Run one Summer League pop-up, backed by lightweight park-court product. In August, sell a hand-painted land-speed numeral tee at DIY Fest. It's the public preview of Salt Line if the 2027-28 slot is approved, or a standalone salt-flats graphic if it is not.
opportunities.segment: Diehards and Gen Z fans tracking prospects
opportunities.kpi: Draft-night e-commerce units in the first 48 hours, Summer League pop-up conversion and land-speed tee sell-through

collection.name: Wasatch Front
collection.story: Built from the strip of land every Jazz fan shares: snow and granite above, salt and lake below, and gyms, all-ages rooms and family courts in between. It makes the gray City Edition feel like Utah, honors the two eras fans already love, and hands the pen to the West Side and DIY scenes.

themes.name: Inversion Layer
themes.story: The winter haze that traps the valley, then the clear blue sky after a storm, turned into the gradient fans see on court. Built for the canyon commute and the cold walk into the arena.
themes.graphics: Vertical gray-to-sky fades, granite-speckle and salt-crackle tonal prints, and a single-line Wasatch ridgeline on hems and liners.
themes.materials: Quilted water-repellent nylon, heavyweight brushed fleece, ripstop shells with snap utility pockets, and baby-blue drawcords and cuffs.

pieces.detail: Charcoal-to-gray baffle fade with a baby-blue zipper pull and a ridgeline-printed liner.
Oversized ripstop shell with a tonal salt-crust print and snap pockets for gym-to-street wear.
Speckled heavyweight fleece with a grid-coordinate sleeve hit in clean sans numerals.
Gray knit with a baby-blue tipped cuff and a small woven Jazz tab.
The same fade in youth and toddler sizes, sold as a set with the adult hoodie.

themes.name: Note, Mountain and Playoff Years
themes.story: The eras Utah argues about, kept apart and treated with respect. That means the Note years in the New Orleans colors, the 1996 Finals-era Mountain, and the Mitchell-Gobert playoff run a younger generation grew up on.
themes.segment: Heritage diehards, fans in their 20s and parents buying for kids
themes.graphics: Licensed original Note and 1996 Mountain marks, never redrawn, in vintage-wash and cracked-ink finishes that echo DI thrift finds. Neck labels and inserts tell the New Orleans origin.
themes.materials: Garment-dyed slub jersey, loopback French terry, tricot warm-ups with snap sleeves, and chain-stitch embroidery.

pieces.detail: Faded purple with the original Note mark and a printed New Orleans 1974 origin neck label.
Tricot warm-up with the 1996 ridgeline in teal and copper piping, licensed through the team.
2017-22 era team marks with a season-by-season playoff date block; no player names unless licensed.
Chain-stitched Note over a gold-and-green rib trim.

themes.name: All-Ages
themes.story: Utah's taste grew up in all-ages rooms, not bars. This theme speaks that language through the gig-poster and flyer culture of Kilby Court, SLUG and Gallery Stroll.
themes.segment: Gen Z fans, the Sugar House and Granary creative crowd
themes.graphics: Two- and three-color off-register screen prints, hand-lettered date blocks for each home month, and cassette and 7-inch sleeve layouts.
themes.materials: Locally screen-printed heavyweight cotton, garment dye, water-based inks, and recycled-board sleeve packaging.

pieces.detail: A different commissioned Utah artist each month, numbered run, artist credited on the hem.
Garment-dyed tee with a cracked-ink 'All-Ages' Jazz lockup.
Record-sleeve packaging with a local-artist playlist QR.
Three pairs in purple, black and sky with a halftone flyer-dot knit.

themes.name: West Side Courts
themes.story: The church gyms, rec centers and family courts of Rose Park, Glendale, West Valley and Kearns, designed by the people who play there.
themes.segment: Pacific Islander and Latino basketball families on the West Side
themes.graphics: Set entirely by paid, credited community designers. Tongan, Samoan and Latino designers each hold credit and approval over their own pieces, and Nike provides the canvas, not the motifs. No tatau, tapa or ceremonial patterns unless the collaborators and their communities choose and approve them.
themes.materials: Durable mesh practice fabrics, heavyweight fleece and family-size runs from youth XS to adult 4XL.

pieces.detail: Reversible mesh with the designer's name and neighborhood on the jock tag.
Long-sleeve shooter with a collaborator-led chest graphic.
Kids' sizes priced for big families, with a share of proceeds to West Side rec leagues.
Outdoor ball with the collaborator's artwork, gifted to local rec programs.

uniform.narrative: The state's namesake lake is shrinking, and its salt crust, shoreline contours and Bonneville land-speed culture are shared Utah icons. A dark shale City Edition with tonal shoreline contours, salt-white numerals and land-speed lettering tells a story only Utah can wear. It stays clear of the white Association uniform and anchors in Mountain Purple. Pitch it now for 2027-28, the first open slot after two seasons of the gray gradient. This season's salt-crackle outerwear and January poster tee are the fan tests. If 2027-28 is already locked, it ships as an August 2027 lifestyle capsule and the uniform moves to 2028-29.
motifs: Tonal shoreline contour lines across a shale body, drawn from Great Salt Lake topography rather than any artwork
Salt-crust crackle texture in the side panels
Hand-painted land-speed numerals and pinstriping from Bonneville Speed Week culture
A single Wasatch ridgeline at the hem, the mountains seen from the lake
uniform.typography: Custom numerals styled on hand-painted land-speed race numbers, in salt white with a thin purple pinstripe outline. A clean sans wordmark with grid-coordinate styling.
details: Jock tag set in Salt Lake grid-coordinate typography, the way locals give directions
North Arm Pink limited to a thin waistband or neck-tape line, and only if fan testing supports it
Neck tape carrying a single ridgeline-to-shoreline line
Court tie-in: a shale baseline band with salt-white shoreline contours
Any lake commitment made through a nonpartisan, science-based Great Salt Lake partner chosen early with the team
avoid: A white or salt-white base that reads like the Association uniform
Repeating the vertical gray gradient or baby-blue trim as the lead story
Replicating Spiral Jetty or any Smithson-derived spiral without Holt-Smithson Foundation engagement
Temple, Temple Square, pioneer-trek or any Latter-day Saint sacred imagery, and Pacific Islander or Native ceremonial patterns
Utah red, BYU blue or Utah State navy, Olympic marks and Utah Mammoth cues that blur team identity

alternates.name: Mardi Gras to the Wasatch
alternates.idea: A purple, gold and green uniform telling the 1974 New Orleans origin and the 1979 move. Build it with a credited New Orleans-side designer so it reads as heritage, not costume.

alternates.name: West Side Courts
alternates.idea: A multi-year community co-creation with Pacific Islander and Latino designers from Rose Park, Glendale and West Valley, with motifs chosen and approved by those communities.

alternates.name: Speed Week
alternates.idea: A shale and chrome uniform built around Bonneville land-speed numerals and pinstripes, a Utah-only hot-rod language.

partners.name: Centro Civico Mexicano
partners.why: A decades-old West Side Latino civic and cultural hub with its own events calendar.
partners.idea: Cultural review for Latino pieces and a sales and launch venue at its community events.

partners.name: Mestizo Institute of Culture and Arts (confirm)
partners.why: A West Side Latino arts organization that could connect the capsule to working Latino designers.
partners.idea: Co-recruit and pay Latino designers for the capsule and the September drop.

partners.name: Salt Lake Arts Council (Living Traditions Festival)
partners.why: Runs Living Traditions and public-art programs that reach Pacific Islander, Latino and other community artists.

partners.name: Craft Lake City
partners.why: Runs the state's busiest maker marketplace and can introduce vetted screen printers and designers.
partners.idea: Curate the monthly Delta Night poster artists and printers, and use DIY Fest to scout the next season.

partners.name: Kilby Court

partners.name: SLUG Magazine
partners.why: Has documented Salt Lake Under Ground for decades, and its poster culture is the graphic reference.

Fridays and Saturdays for in-person drops. Sundays, Halloween and General Conference weekends go digital only.

risks.risk: Most dated hooks beyond Oct 30 are unconfirmed: the second home Cup date, any legend night, Rising Stars picks and 2027 festival dates.
risks.mitigation: Anchor every priority-1 plan to dates already certain: Oct 17, Oct 30, Black Friday, Dec 1 to Jan 6. Run each conditional beat on pre-approved blanks with a named fallback. Confirm the purple, black and sky blue hexes with the team before colorways lock.

risks.risk: City Edition fatigue in a second season of the same gray gradient.
risks.mitigation: Sell it as material and outerwear, never as new, and announce the next City Edition direction early.

risks.risk: Cultural missteps with Pacific Islander, Latino, Native or Latter-day Saint imagery, or with the state's religious culture as a punchline.
risks.mitigation: Co-create only with paid, credited designers, and give each community its own approval. Keep church and temple imagery and drink or diet jokes out. Run cultural review before sampling.

risks.risk: Licensing gaps on heritage jerseys and marks, Stockton, Malone, Sloan, Maravich and Mitchell names, and Smithson-derived imagery.
risks.mitigation: Confirm the heritage-jersey licensee, and clear team, NBA, NBPA and estate rights first. Where rights are uncertain, use team marks and unbranded cues (salt texture, ridgelines).

risks.risk: Rebuild volatility: a slow start or deadline move can swing demand between Peterson, Bailey, Markkanen and Jackson Jr.
risks.mitigation: Hold player-specific depth on youth tees and keep fast-print capacity. Clear Kessler stock before Oct 17, and re-weight after the first month and at the Feb 11 deadline.

scorecard.rationale: A small metro, but the buyer base is the whole state: family-sized, youth-heavy and loyal to one team. Its design vocabulary is unusually distinct (salt, snow, all-ages DIY, West Side hoops). Retail is spread along I-15 with a thin boutique layer, and a rebuild year with no national stage caps the near-term upside.
